payload.summary: ROOT CAUSE FOUND: model arch (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration) IS supported by installed vLLM 0.28.0+rocm723 and weights load fine; boot dies in profile_run at the first FP8 dense linear with 'torch._scaled_mm is only supported on CUDA devices with compute capability >= 9.0 or 8.9, or ROCm MI300+'. Host is 8x MI250X (gfx90a, CDNA2) which has NO hardware FP8 MMA. vLLM's ROCm kernel registry falls through aiter (disabled/CDNA3+), ROCmFP8ScaledMM (CDNA3+ gate), PerTensor/RowWise torch gates, and lands on ChannelWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel whose is_supported() cc>=89 gate is fooled by gfx90a reporting capability (9,0). Working on a Triton FP8 w8a8 per-token/per-channel bridging kernel patch.

new_findings.what: gfx90a reports torch compute capability (9,0) = cc 90, so vLLM's TorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported(cc<89) gate wrongly passes on MI250X and torch._scaled_mm then aborts at runtime
new_findings.expected_impact: Explains the whole 'unknown' boot failure; fixes mis-selection of a hardware-FP8 kernel on a non-FP8 arch

new_findings.what: Triton tl.dot on float8_e4m3fn inputs DOES execute on gfx90a (Triton 3.7.1; ~9.7 TFLOPS native-fp8 path, ~32 TFLOPS when upcast to bf16), so a Triton FP8 w8a8 GEMM is a viable enablement bridge where torch._scaled_mm is not
new_findings.expected_impact: Unblocks boot without dequantizing ~400GB of FP8 weights to BF16 (which would OOM: 8x64GB HBM)
new_findings.accuracy_risk: low (fp32 accumulate, per-token/per-channel dequant identical to the intended ChannelWiseTorch math)
